thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — we're planning a staggered release across API, runtime, console, and router during Wed 00:00-04:00 UTC. Goal is minimal blast radius, we need a handshake order and a clear rollback lattice. Deploybot will orchestrate waves.

alex: timeline + which service goes first? I assume API -> runtime -> router -> console?

maya: thinking API (v2.14 pinned) -> runtime (v3.8 roll) -> router (route-table change) -> console last. Need to confirm compatible model variants for runtime fallback.

sam: we should avoid changing runtime kernel selection during the window. If we need a kernel flip, do it later — that's a high-risk op.

chloe: agree. also want per-service canary slices: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> full. console canary can run in parallel with router 10% stage.

alex: for pins: API will stay pinned to 2.14 for the window; runtime will accept v3.8 and v3.7 fallback. Router must have rev back to 1.9 of header-split. Put that in release notes.

maya: noted. I'll add the rollback lattice: if runtime health < 95% for 5m, rollback runtime to v3.7 and route traffic to replica pool in us-east. If API errors spike, route back to 2.13 and pause runtime progression.

deploybot: PRE-FLIGHT: running checks: config-lock, schema-compat, dep-graph, infra-capacity.

deploybot: PRE-FLIGHT RESULTS: config-lock OK, schema-compat WARNING (console schema has optional field mismatch), dep-graph OK, infra-capacity OK.

chloe: the schema mismatch is only for an optional telemetry field; console can ignore for now but add feature-flag guard.

sam: can we add a quick KV eviction safety net? In past router changes caused cache churn, leading to runtime slowdown. Recommend increased cache TTLs during ramp.

maya: add TTL bump for router-cache and enable conservative eviction on runtime. I'll update the playbook.

alex: what are our monitoring thresholds that will auto-trigger rollback? Need explicit values for on-call.

opsbot: ALERT RULES (for this window): error-rate > 2% sustained for 3m -> page #platform-oncall; p50 latency increase > 40% over baseline for 5m -> notify #infra; runtime OOM > 2 instances in 10m -> auto-rollback runtime.

maya: good. Also adding manual abort condition: any customer-facing outage observed by CS -> immediate pause and rollback to last pinned stable across all services.

chloe: release notes draft (very short): "Staged rollout: API 2.14 (pinned), Runtime 3.8 (with 3.7 fallback), Router header-split update, Console minor telemetry schema change behind flag. Expect transient 1xx redirects during header swap."

alex: can we have a simple command to run rollback for each service? put commands in runbook.

maya: yeah — adding these snippets to the playbook:

maya: ```
# rollback runtime to 3.7
deploybot rollback --service runtime --to-version 3.7 --reason "health spike"
# pin API to 2.13
deploybot pin --service api --version 2.13 --note "emergency rollback"
```

sam: :thumbsup: will test rollback snippets in staging.

deploybot: SCHEDULED: Wave 1 (API) start 00:10 UTC, Wave 2 (runtime) start 00:30 UTC, Wave 3 (router) start 01:10 UTC, Wave 4 (console) start 02:00 UTC. Dry-run for canary at 00:05.

maya: thanks — I'll update the release doc and handoff to oncall. Please ack if you reviewed and are comfortable.

chloe: ack

alex: ack. I'll keep an eye on API metrics during the first 20m.

sam: ack, will monitor runtime memory and cache eviction metrics.

opsbot: REMINDER: quiet-window reserved 00:00-04:00 UTC. Non-critical changes blocked.

maya: ended — thanks everyone. Posting runbook link in release notes. :party_parrot:
